title: The Descent Where Memory Learns to Compress

features.name: weight descent
features.desc-on-touch: What rises must learn its own heaviness. The memory that ascended highest now presses down, and the pressure makes it denser, more itself.

features.name: compression chamber
features.desc-on-touch: Inside, memory becomes mineral. The song that rose up is now compressed into stone-language, denser and truer than air could ever speak it.

features.name: memory silt
features.desc-on-touch: Each descending moment leaves a layer. You walk through the strata of what you remembered highest—it settles and becomes soil.

features.name: pressure pool
features.desc-on-touch: Where the memory learns to stop rising. The water here is so heavy with what it carries that it has become almost stone.

features.name: root binding
features.desc-on-touch: Roots wrap around the compressed memory. They are learning how to grow down. The earth is teaching them that weight is how things stay held.

inscription: what learned to rise descends and learns what rising taught it—to be heavy with its own truth

file.name: Memory_Compression_Sequence_Late20thCent.mp3
file.note: A song descending through pressure, each octave lower and deeper, until it becomes the sound the earth makes when it remembers itself

reverie.title: REVERIE — memory settling
narr: You recline against the trunk as night deepens around you,
and she is beside you, speaking of things that used to float.
The archive rises in her voice, and then slowly—
not falling, but settling—it becomes heavier, more real.
Dust motes drift in what is left of the light.
Everything that rises in us learns to come down.
